home_hero_heading: View and edit Exif data locally
home_feature_private_description: Images never leave your browser and are {#em}never{/em} uploaded to someone else's server
home_feature_standardized_description: Uses the WebAssembly library {#link href=$libexifWasmUrl}libexif-wasm{/link} based on the {#link href=$libexifUrl}libexif{/link} C library, which supports all of Exif standard 2.1 and most of 2.2
home_feature_convenient_description: Read and write Exif data directly in the browser
home_faq_what_answer: exifi is an open-source (MIT) tool to view and edit Exif data in the browser. It uses the C library {#link href=$libexifUrl}libexif{/link} compiled to WebAssembly ({#link href=$libexifWasmUrl}libexif-wasm{/link}). It also makes use of the following C libraries for image writing: {#link href=$libjpegUrl}libjpeg{/link}, {#link href=$libpngUrl}libpng{/link}, {#link href=$libwebpUrl}libwebp{/link}, and {#link href=$libheifUrl}libheif{/link}.
home_faq_formats_answer: JPEG images, PNG images, WebP images, and raw Exif metadata files are supported. HEIC, HEIF, and AVIF images are supported on a read-only basis. For more information, see {#link href=$issueUrl}jeremy-code/exifi#13{/link}.
home_faq_specialized_question: Why should I use this over a specialized tool like ExifTool or Adobe Lightroom?
home_faq_specialized_answer: Realistically, if you are a photographer or someone who edits images frequently, you probably should be using a specialized tool for the job. These may include: {#link href=$exifToolUrl}ExifTool{/link} by Phil Harvey, {#link href=$darktableUrl}darktable{/link}, {#link href=$lightroomUrl}Adobe Lightroom{/link}, or many other software. This is more of a service for those who want to quickly add a little bit of metadata to their images quickly online without having to upload them to someone's server.
home_faq_metadata_question: What image metadata can be viewed or edited?
home_faq_metadata_answer: Only the Exif standard 2.1 and most of 2.2 are supported. Other metadata that may be stored, such as XMP, is not supported. This also means that Exif data defined by the XMP namespace for Exif ({#link href=$xmpExifUrl}EXIF namespace{/link}) is also not supported. For more information on the Exif specification, see the Wikipedia article on {#link href=|https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exif|}Exif{/link} or view the official Exif 2.21 standard published by JEITA {#link href=$jeitaUrl}at this URL{/link} (or in {#link href=$jeitaJapaneseUrl}Japanese{/link}).
home_faq_link_question: How do I read Exif data from a link?
home_faq_link_answer: You can open a link with a URL search parameter like this: {#viewerLink url=$viewerUrl}{viewerUrl}{/viewerLink}.
home_faq_offline_answer: Yes! exifi can be used as a progressive web app ({#abbr}PWA{/abbr}). For more information on how to install a PWA, see this guide by MDN: {#link href=|https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Progressive_web_apps/Guides/Installing|}Installing and uninstalling web apps{/link}.
home_faq_tags_question: What are some useful tags someone may want to add?
home_faq_tags_text_item: Tags that provide additional textual information include: ImageDescription, Artist, Copyright, XPTitle, XPAuthor, XPKeywords, XPSubject, and CameraOwnerName
home_faq_tags_gps_item: GPS data such as Longitude, Latitude can be added or edited accordingly in the "Edit GPS" menu
home_faq_tags_date_item: DateTime/OffsetTime or their variants, DateTimeOriginal/OffsetTimeOriginal or DateTimeDigitized/OffsetTimeDigitized can also be edited
home_faq_tags_full_list_link: A full list of tags can be found here.
home_faq_ifd_intro: An Image File Domain ({#abbr}IFD{/abbr}) refers to the type of data an Exif entry pertains to. There are five IFDs for Exif data:
home_faq_ifd_ifd0_item: {#strong}IFD 0{/strong} refers to the main data regarding the image (X or Y-Resolution, ImageDescription, Model, etc.).
home_faq_ifd_ifd1_item: {#strong}IFD 1{/strong} refers to data regarding the thumbnail of the image. If a tag is available in both IFD 0 and IFD 1, you probably want to put it in IFD 0.
home_faq_ifd_exif_item: The {#strong}Exif IFD{/strong} refers to additional miscellaneous metadata on the image (e.g. ExifVersion, ColorSpace, ExposureTime, etc.).
home_faq_ifd_gps_item: The {#strong}GPS IFD{/strong} refers to geographic data relevant to the image (e.g. Latitude, Longitude).
home_faq_ifd_interoperability_item: The {#strong}Interoperability IFD{/strong} refers to interoperability tags (InteroperabilityIndex and/or InteroperabilityVersion).
home_faq_makernote_answer: MakerNote data is stored in a special tag in the Exif IFD reserved exclusively for manufacturer-specific binary data. For more information, see {#link href=$wikipediaUrl}Wikipedia:Exif#MakerNote data{/link}. Currently, libexif is able to decode the following manufacturers: {#link href=$canonUrl}Canon{/link}, {#link href=$fujiUrl}Fuji{/link}, {#link href=$olympusUrl}Olympus{/link} (Epson, Sanyo), and {#link href=$pentaxUrl}Pentax{/link} (Casio) .
home_faq_png_question: Why is exifi not correctly reading my PNG's Exif data?
home_faq_png_answer: In July 2017, {#link href=$specUrl}version 1.5.0 of the extensions to the PNG 1.2 Specification{/link} added support for an eXIf chunk in PNGs that stored Exif metadata. Previously, legacy encoders stored Exif data in nonstandard methods. For example, ImageMagick stored Exif information in a "Raw profile type APP1" zTXt chunk, whereas Photoshop stored it in a "Raw profile type exif" zTXt chunk. Furthermore, some PNG encoders will, when converting from JPEG, choose to encode Exif data as XMP data under the {#link href=$xmpExifUrl}EXIF namespace{/link}. Since read and write support for PNGs is handled by libpng reading the eXIf chunk specifically, you may experience false negatives for older PNGs where exifi claims that an image has no Exif data when it was actually stored somewhere else.
home_faq_remove_question: I am looking for a web app to remove all metadata from my photos; is exifi for me?
home_faq_remove_answer: No, exifi is only capable of reading Exif metadata and not other forms of metadata such as XMP. You probably should look towards something like Google Chrome Lab's {#link href=$squooshUrl}squoosh.app{/link}, which also uses WebAssembly to handle image encoding directly in the browser and, most importantly, {#em}only{/em} preserves image data.
